item.title: Centillion to the power of a centillion, or a googolplex?
Sam wants your RAM
item.description: Sam Altman: “But from a global allocation perspective, actually it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer” From an allocation perspective, actually it seems quite terrible that the richest 100 US billionaires own more than 7 trillion dollar, sitting on more wealth than 70% of US households combined, while many have to struggle to get health care, education, nutrition and shelter.

item.title: Zur Ontologischen Bestimmung Neuronaler Netze
item.description: 2003, 2004 schrieb ich als Philosophiestudent eine Hausarbeit über Neuronale Netze, Turingvollständigkeit, und die Frage, was Künstliche Intelligenz und den Menschen ausmachen. Damals ging es um Ray Kurzweils Visionen, die Grenzen künstlicher Intelligenz und die Möglichkeit, den menschlichen Geist auf einem Computer nachzubilden. Mehr als zwanzig Jahre später, im Zeitalter von LLMs und generativer KI, habe ich die Arbeit wiederveröffentlicht. Manche meiner Argumente würde ich heute anders formulieren, einige Aussagen korrigieren, aber ein paar Gedanken sind vielleicht interessant.

item.title: Does the Truth feed those people?
item.description: I looked up something that sounded like a quote using Google: “Does the truth feed those people?” Google’s AI answered, without even a single Web search result beneath, *only* the AI answer: “Does the truth feed those people?” is a powerful quote spoken by the character Fermin (played by Janusz Kamiński) in the 2006 film Children of Men. Which would be a great answer. If that was a quote from the film.

item.title: Checking one fact: Yelena in Brand New Day
item.description: This is not really about Spider-Man, but about the Truth, about AI, and Wikipedia. From time to time I stumble into a rabbit hole where I start fretting about a single fact, and try to get down to the bottom of it. Sometimes I write about these (e.g. the height of Anson Mount, or the place of birth of Ena Begović). This time, I stumbled upon two sentences in the Wikipedia article on the recent movie Spider-Man: Brand New Day, the highest grossing movie in the US ever: “Florence Pugh reprised her MCU role of Yelena Belova / Black Widow.

item.title: Updating Simia
item.description: The last few days, the Website was going really slow again. And I was preparing for a frustrating fight with Bitnami, Google Cloud, and whatever else to figure things out. I have to admit that this is not what happened. Google Cloud has a Gemini-powered Cloud Assist chatbot. And I just asked it what to do. The suggestions sounded reasonable, and it wrote down the exact commands. A few times I came to an error, but just copy-pasting it to the assistant, it quickly found out what to do instead, and, well, it seemed to have worked.

item.title: Mega-IPOs
item.description: There are more than 15 trillion (!) dollar invested in index funds. Starting in a few days and going on until the fall of next year, more than half a trillion dollar of that money will be pulled out from the existing company shares in numerous indexes and used to buy SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic shares from their existing share owners. (Most of it will start happening in about a year, when the S&P500 lets SpaceX join.

item.title: The Future of Truth
item.description: What a mind boggling and raw article by Wired: Steve Rosenbaum has a book out, “The Future of Truth”, on the effect of AI chatbots on the understanding of truth. Rosenbaum has a master’s degree in “truth” from New York University (what does that even mean?) and has decades of experience in this field: creating news programs for MTV and reporting on the aftermath of 9/11 in New York and much more.

item.title: The Web attacked by AI
item.description: The Web I grew up with and that grew up with me was already slowly fading. The Web of many people and organizations having their own small website. Capitalism and convenience lead to a concentration onto a small number of platforms and apps, but mostly these platforms let the rest be. People and small organizations and groups could still have their little website. But the ongoing indiscriminate onslaught of AI bots on everything with an URL is just actively killing the web and its open nature.

item.title: Question about Economics (as a discipline)
item.description: Serious and honest question, and I’m not trying to diss on a different discipline: I don’t have much experience reading papers in economics. And I saw that paper “AI, Human Cognition and Knowledge Collapse”, on a topic that I find very interesting, written by Acemoğlu et al. Now, Acemoğlu is a Nobel prize winner and MIT professor, so I would assume that paper is among the best economics would offer on that subject.

item.title: Pretraining biases
item.description: “A rose by any other name would smell as sweet” – not in a world of LLMs, though, because whenever you fine tune the LLM to your task, you have to always consider what it has already learned in the initial pre-training.

item.title: Technoblade in different language Wikipedias
item.description: One thing I really like to do is to compare the articles in different language editions of Wikipedia about the same topic (I know, I’m a nerd). My daughter was watching me doing that, and then she suggested a topic, and she suggested we should ask an AI to help us. The topic she suggested was the YouTuber Technoblade, whose article is available in 35 different language editions of Wikipedia, and I decided on using Gemini since I got a free subscription for its paid-tier service for a year when I bought a new phone recently.

item.title: OpenAI gets into shopping
item.description: OpenAI and Perplexity, armed with significant AI capabilities, have targeted the shopping domain. And have run into many problems around data access and semantics. This raises three thoughts: First, companies which are bullish about AI “changing everything”, are stumbling in maybe the most traditional, mundane domain: shopping. This doesn’t inspire confidence in their technology. Second, companies which speak of ushering in the singularity in just a few months, are dedicating person-years of engineering to a conventional market.

item.title: Cancelling a car repair appointment
Tech companies and the size of the market
item.description: If you think there might be an AI bubble, but don’t worry about it, even if it pops, how bad can it be? Here’s one number: seven tech companies (NVIDIA, Microsoft, Google, Apple, Meta, Tesla and Amazon) are worth about 20 trillion together, representing a third of the value of the total US stock market. For context: total subprime mortgages in 2008 were 1.3 trillion, total US mortgage debt was 10 trillion.

item.title: Additions with unique digits: a tale of puzzling and AI
item.description: The other day, Markus Krötzsch and I were catching up when one of his kids came in. She told us about a puzzle her math teacher gave her: How many integer sums are there where the equation uses each digit at most once? The simplest example is 1+2=3, but 12+47=59 also works. On the other hand, 1+9=10 isn’t a solution because the digit ‘1’ appears twice (in the first number and the sum).

item.title: Ontologische Bestimmung Neuronaler Netze
item.description: „Für Trubel und hitzige Diskussionen sorgte in der letzten Runde des Turniers auch die Partie von Shredder: In klar gewonnener Stellung ließ der spätere Champion eine dreifache Stellungswiederholung zu. Sein Gegner hätte nach den Schachregeln daraufhin die Partie für Unentschieden erklären lassen können. Dies empfand er aber in verlorener Stellung als unfair, spielte weiter und verlor schließlich. Gut für Shredder, schlecht für Fritz, das im Falle eines Unentschiedens Weltmeister gewesen wäre, so aber in den Stichkampf mußte und diesen auch noch verlor.
